name: Why kappa = 1/2
data: κ in a₀ = κc√(Gρ), measured from the combined local a₀ of CFG493's three routes (P1 SPARC gas points, P2 MeerKAT MIGHTEE-HI widths, P3 WALLABY DR2), re-fitted by S3 step by step for v3 (kernel ν₁, AQUAL disc geometry, host field). κ_Λ uses ρ_Λ, κ_crit uses ρ_crit. D5 enumerates de Sitter horizon constructions.
picture: κ_Λ (dark) and κ_crit (blue) with 1σ errors after each re-fit step. Red line: κ = ½, the fitted value the framework uses. Grey dashed line: Z/4π, which is Milgrom's cH_Λ/2π, the simplest value horizon thermodynamics gives (a postulate, not ½).
why: With v3's AQUAL disc geometry, κ_Λ = 0.499 ± 0.116 and κ_crit = 0.413 ± 0.096: both are consistent with ½ but the error (about 0.1) cannot tell ½ from Z/4π or neighbouring values, so the data do not discriminate. On the theory side, D5 proves that products of horizon quantities give κ² = rational × odd power of π, so ½ is never reached; with square roots ½ appears only as 'κ = 1 times a half picked from a menu'. κ = ½ is therefore FITTED, and why it is ½ stays open.

name: Stiffness length L*
data: D10: velocity dispersions of four outer Milky Way globulars (NGC 2419, Pal 3, Pal 4, Pal 14), each solved as a Plummer sphere in the Galaxy's field with v3's stiffened field equation, scanned in L*. C3: the length scales of AeST's own action (mass term μ, r_C, curl length).
picture: Left: Δχ² of the globulars against L* for both footings; the leftmost point is L* = 0 (plain AQUAL); dashed lines mark the 95 % floor; the yellow band is the 20–90 pc window. Right: log bar chart of the floor and window top against AeST's own length scales (canonical).
why: Plain AQUAL (L* = 0) is excluded by the globulars and no finite L* beats Newton, so the data give only a lower bound: L* ≥ 21.68 / 22.85 pc with SPS mass-to-light ratios (2.9–23.8 pc across the M/L and MW-field brackets). The upper edge near 90 pc comes from the window used in the lanes, not from a fit here. C3 shows no term in AeST's class makes such a short length: its scales start at kiloparsecs and its equivalent length √2/μ is ≥ 1.41 Mpc. So L* is a new constant, FITTED, and its origin is open.

name: What sets the cold-mass amount
data: CFG886 rebuilds the cold-to-baryon ratio R = ω_c/ω_b from DESI DR2 BAO + BBN deuterium (and a SH0ES H₀ variant, and a free-dark-energy scan) without the Planck fit. U1 solves v3's dust equilibria for 137 system-footing cases (satellites, Coma UDGs, TDGs, DF2/DF4) and asks how much dust v3 can hold.
picture: Left: R from the three CFG886 routes (points with 1σ, the free-DE range as a bar) against the 5.364 input the lanes use (dashed). Right: U1's largest held-dust-to-phantom mass ratio for isotropic and anisotropic dust, and the median held fraction for hosted satellites; the red line at 1 is the law's phantom.
why: In v3 (C2, C4) the dust abundance is a free initial condition, so nothing in the theory sets it; the value 5.364 is an input taken from Planck's ΛCDM fit (inherited input). CFG886 recovers 5.27 ± 0.22 only by assuming constant dark energy, gets 6.12 ± 0.32 with the local H₀, and with free dark energy BAO + BBN allow 2.95–8.06: not pinned. Locally, U1's theorem T1 says held dust never exceeds the phantom (largest ratio 0.666 over 14,373 equilibria; radial anisotropy β > ¼ can exceed it only near the centre, not shown), and T3 says hosted systems hold none. The amount is not derived anywhere.

name: Law + a^1 growth + no EFE, local
data: A theory statement (CFG946 theorem: a local second-order field that gives the profile-independent deep law must carry an external-field effect), checked for v3 by F3: linear σ8 of v3's Khronon dust as a function of its mass μ_K, for two kernels and two start times, and the EFE cost on dwarf satellites (F3's 1-D estimate, S1's solved value).
picture: Left: linear σ8 relative to the dust limit at three μ_K values per kernel (log axis). Green: μ_K allowed by BS24's Eq. 39 cap; red: μ_K needed for σ8 within 5 % (dashed line). The two never meet. Right: the boost the satellites lose to the external field (F3 estimate vs S1's solve).
why: The no-go says no local theory can have the law, standard a¹ growth and no EFE at once. v3 does not dodge it: it pays the no-EFE leg by having an EFE (which costs the satellites 0.58 / 0.57 dex, about twice F3's 1-D estimate), and the growth leg comes back as an empty μ_K window: growth needs μ_K ≥ 361–2542 h/Mpc, the cap is 14.8, a gap of 24–172×. Inherited inputs: F3's linear runs use Planck-2018 initial conditions and a flat w = −1 background (ΛCDM-processed).

name: Radiative stability (G12)
data: CFG320's gate G12 on the old filtered C-H/K chassis: an 81-point grid of the couplings α_c and c₂, each with its own strong-coupling cutoff Λ_sc, and the Lorentz-violation leakage into matter from loops (EFT piece) and from a worst-case UV completion, against a 2σ bound from Klinkhamer & Schreck 2008 (marked provisional in the lane). The board tile is grey: not yet recomputed for v3 (N0 audit row 54).
picture: Log-log scatter over the 81 grid points: EFT leakage (dark dots) and worst-case UV leakage (open red) against each point's cutoff, the bound as a dashed line, and the condition M_* ≤ 9.9e8 GeV as a vertical line.
why: On the old chassis the theory is natural (loop corrections to the couplings stay tiny) and the EFT leakage is at least 40 times under the bound at every point, but a worst-case UV completion passes at only 3 of 81 points. So the old verdict was conditional: new UV physics must enter below about 1e9 GeV. v3 also has a preferred foliation, so this bound must be redone with v3's own couplings (batch R5); until then the tile is grey and the old numbers are shown only as the record.

name: Covariant completion
data: No data arrays: a theory tile. Three lanes form the trilemma: C3 (AeST's own length scales), I1 (principal symbol and Cauchy problem of the γ_L stiffness term on twisting and untwisted aethers), F3 (linear growth of the untwisted v3 Khronon), with C7 (v4 = AeST + γ_L in a patched CLASS) for the twisted option on FRW.
picture: Three boxes, one per horn, each with its deciding number, and arrows showing how fixing one horn forces the next; the centre names the one escape still open.
why: A covariant parent must (1) screen the law on small scales, which needs the added stiffness term γ_L because AeST's own scales are all far too large; (2) keep the field equations well-posed, but I1 shows γ_L is well-posed only where the aether is twist-free, and a disc galaxy or the Sun in the Galaxy forces twist; (3) the twist-free choice is v3's Khronon, whose linear growth fails (no allowed μ_K window), while the twisted v4 runs away on FRW (C7). Only a native nonlinear v3 simulation could still rescue growth; until it runs, the completion fails.
